clue.text: Plays around with better paper

parts.note: to fool with something is to play around with it, so the phrase gives FOOLS
to cap a story is to better or outdo it

explanation.surface: Someone fiddling with a superior grade of writing paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' looks like an adjective describing the paper, but it is the verb meaning outdo.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a traditional large size of writing or printing sheet, named after its old fool's-cap watermark.

clue.text: Sporadic outbreak of flu coming after match

indicators.note: coming after means the rearranged letters follow the word for match

parts.note: two things that match fit together

indicators.note: an outbreak scatters and breaks things up, so the letters of flu are rearranged

explanation.surface: A patchy flu epidemic arriving after a sports fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming in irregular bursts or spells, as in broken sleep, means sporadic.

clue.text: One speaks for a Tory — to a limited extent

indicators.note: to a limited extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone speaks up for a Conservative, though only partly.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A public speaker, someone who delivers formal addresses, is one who speaks.

clue.text: The bench arranged an area for driving

parts.note: something set out has been arranged
a tee is the area on a golf course where players drive off

explanation.surface: The judges organised a zone for motoring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The bench' suggests judges and 'driving' suggests cars; the driving is golf, from the tee.
explanation.definitionFit: A sofa for two or more people is a padded bench-like seat.

clue.text: Superior food that's without deceit

parts.note: something superior is above another
board means food, as in room and board

explanation.surface: Fine cuisine that is honestly presented.
explanation.definitionFit: Honest and open dealings are legitimate and free of trickery.

clue.text: Require theologian to accept return call

indicators.note: to accept means the theologian's letters take the other piece inside them

parts.note: DD stands for Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree

indicators.note: return asks for the word for call to be read backwards

parts.note: to call someone something is to name them

explanation.surface: A divinity scholar is required to take a phone call back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'call' looks like a phone call, but it is the verb to name someone; a theologian is a Doctor of Divinity.
explanation.definitionFit: To insist on something as a right or need is to call for it, a synonym of require.

clue.text: Why do oxen tire out?

indicators.note: out means the letters of oxen tire are put out of order

explanation.surface: Asking why working cattle become exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges OXEN TIRE; the whole clue is also the definition, since hard labour is why oxen tire.
explanation.definitionFit: Strenuous physical effort is what wears out draught animals.

clue.text: French words are so long!

parts.note: seems to complain about lengthy vocabulary, but so long is a farewell, and the clue asks for the French way of saying it

explanation.definitionFit: It is the French parting phrase meaning goodbye until we meet again.

clue.text: Arranging to fill the window table?

definitions.text: Arranging to fill the window table?

parts.words: Arranging to fill the window table?
parts.note: one word fits all three: arranging, the display that fills a shop window, and a bedroom table with a mirror

explanation.definitionFit: Dressing a shop window arranges goods, and a bedroom table with a mirror carries the same name.

clue.text: Fighting against case of terror, and getting a grip

indicators.note: against means the word for fighting is set beside the case of terror, coming after it
the case of a word is its outside shell, so its first and last letters are taken

parts.note: fighting in a war is action, as in soldiers seeing action

explanation.surface: Battling against an outbreak of terror while trying to keep control.
explanation.walkthrough: The first and last letters of 'terror' are T and R.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names the grip a wheel or tyre holds on a road surface.

clue.text: The beloved compiler's expression of dismay

parts.note: a loved one is called a dear
the compiler of a crossword refers to themself as me; the possessive adds no letters

explanation.surface: A crossword setter's sweetheart, voicing disappointment.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often call themselves 'this compiler' or 'me' in clues, so 'compiler' gives ME.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a mild exclamation of regret or surprise, like 'oh dear'.

clue.text: One end up, perhaps, and not yet broken

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the words One end up could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A box standing on one end may still be sealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the eight letters of ONE END UP.
explanation.definitionFit: A seal, packet or letter not yet broken into is still intact and closed.

clue.text: Staff's time put into rescues

definitions.note: read as staffs, the plural; the definition is a plural noun

indicators.note: put into means the letter for time is placed inside the word for rescues

parts.note: to rescue someone is to save them

explanation.surface: Office workers' hours are spent on rescue missions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff's' looks like a possessive, but it stands for the plural of staff, sticks or poles.
explanation.definitionFit: The old plural of staff, a walking stick or pole, is staves.

clue.text: Deceptive trick by undercover us cops? Ouch!

indicators.note: undercover agents are disguised, so the letters of us cops and ouch appear in disguise

explanation.surface: An American police sting goes painfully wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a conjuror's patter, used for any trickery or deception.

clue.text: Put a proposal against crazy movement

indicators.note: against means the proposal is set beside the crazy word, after it

parts.note: loco is slang for crazy, from Spanish
a proposal put to a meeting is a motion

explanation.surface: Tabling a motion opposing something mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put' is only a joining word; 'against' means beside.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a general term for moving from place to place, as in animal travel.

clue.text: Speed reduced — that's a blow!

parts.note: speed is slang for amphetamine, a stimulant drug also called an upper
prices reduced are cut

explanation.surface: Cutting a speed limit, which comes as a shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speed' looks like velocity but is the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer's upward punch to the chin is a kind of blow.

clue.text: Campaign for instant acceptance of victory in Europe

indicators.note: acceptance of means the word for instant takes the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: an instant is a moment
VE stands for Victory in Europe, as in VE Day in 1945

explanation.surface: Lobbying for immediate recognition of a European triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: An organised campaign for a cause, such as the peace drive, is a political movement.

clue.text: A little money precedes little craving

indicators.note: precedes means the money letter comes before the word for little

parts.note: P stands for penny, a small coin
petite means small or little

explanation.surface: A small sum comes before a small desire.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong desire for food or anything else is a hunger or craving.

clue.text: How might us poor reps get rich?

indicators.note: the question asks in what other way the words us poor reps could appear, which signals rearranging them

explanation.surface: Poorly paid sales representatives wondering how to make their fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How might' rearranges the ten letters of US POOR REPS; 'get' is a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: Wealthy and flourishing people are well off, the same as rich.

clue.text: When might answer be found in heavenly food?

definitions.note: the answer is a reply to when, meaning at some later time

indicators.note: be found in means the letter for answer sits inside the word for heavenly food

parts.note: manna is the food sent from heaven to the Israelites in the Bible

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the answer lies in food from heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might' is a joining word; the Spanish word is a vague promise of 'tomorrow', the reply to 'When?'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish reply meaning tomorrow or some time later answers the question of timing.

clue.text: How one might see there's no sulphur in wine?

indicators.note: there's no means the letter for sulphur is missing from the wine

parts.note: retsina is a Greek resin-flavoured white wine
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: Checking a glass of wine for sulphites by eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye is the organ of sight.

clue.text: Agreed to cover copyright without delay

indicators.note: to cover means the phrase for agreed goes around the copyright symbol

parts.note: people at one are in agreement
C is the copyright symbol

explanation.surface: Consenting to protect intellectual property promptly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cover' puts C inside AT ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Immediately or straight away means acting the moment something is asked.

clue.text: Back the French regular team

indicators.note: back means the French word for the is read in reverse

parts.note: le is French for the
even means regular or steady, as in an even pace

explanation.surface: Supporting the French national side.
explanation.definitionFit: A side in football or cricket has this many players, so the number stands for a team.

clue.text: A mother, for example, welcomes parking that's clear

indicators.note: welcomes means the word for mother takes the parking letter inside it

parts.note: a mother is one example of a parent
P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs

explanation.surface: A mum greeting a car-parking space that is free.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obvious or plain to see is evident, as is anything clear.

clue.text: Clergyman belonging to the magic circle?

indicators.note: magic suggests the letters of circle are transformed into something new

explanation.surface: A priest who is a member of a club of conjurors.
explanation.walkthrough: The Magic Circle is a famous British society of magicians; here 'magic' rearranges CIRCLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman is a priest or minister, a member of the clergy.

clue.text: Cause for a party?

definitions.meaning: a cause or reason for something
a special event or celebration such as a party

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a reason or grounds and a special social event.

clue.text: Sit back collecting the taxes

indicators.note: collecting means the reversed word gathers the other word inside it
back means the word sit is read backwards

explanation.surface: Relax while the tax collector gathers your dues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sit back' looks like an invitation to relax, but 'back' turns the word round, giving TIS to hold the article.
explanation.definitionFit: These were levies of a tenth of produce paid to the church, a form of tax.

clue.text: Adventure these days lies in flight

indicators.note: lies in means the abbreviation sits inside the word for flight

parts.note: flight from danger is an escape
AD, anno Domini, marks the present era, these days

explanation.surface: Modern life is full of daring getaways.
explanation.definitionFit: A reckless or daring exploit is a madcap adventure.
